audience: Training coordinators, departmental representatives and synthetic reviewing operators preparing a fictional weekly PB4T meeting offline.
primaryTask: Inspect fictional proposals and policy, optimize a deconflicted weekly drill calendar, review all required occurrences and crew loads, correct conflicts, then accept and export the exact synthetic revision.
successOutcome: Every required occurrence is covered by a qualified, available, conflict-free allocation under explicit synthetic fatigue rules; five agent responses and named reports explain the result; deliberate synthetic acceptance binds to the saved valid revision and survives reload.

screens.name: PB4T workspace
screens.purpose: Load a labeled synthetic week; inspect/edit roster, operations, resources, proposals, history, search budget and versioned fatigue/recurrence policy.

screens.name: Weekly PB4T Schedule Board
screens.purpose: Show Monday–Sunday assignments, cross-week required occurrences, initial collisions, bounded search status, competing saved/draft edits and correction paths.

screens.name: Reports and synthetic review
screens.purpose: Review Departmental Negotiation Log, Conflict and Resolution Report, Periodicity Coverage Report, Personnel Loading Heatmap and Synthetic Schedule Review Record and Export.

states.empty: On first open show the synthetic-only warning and Load synthetic sample; no accepted schedule or invented history. Empty reports explain the next action. Confirm replacement/reset of nonempty work with explicit in-page confirm/cancel controls.
states.loading: Validate locally first; show Searching and node budget, disable duplicate Optimize actions, keep Stop search reachable. Yield between bounded search chunks; allow a visible stop before committing results. Once Stop is requested, discard any uncommitted result and preserve drafts and the last valid revision.
states.error: Show field-specific input errors and occurrence-specific conflicts inline with a linked summary. Distinguish invalid input, infeasible over supplied candidates, search exhausted and stopped. Keep uncovered/overdue drills visible. Preserve draft controls and last valid board; stale results must be visibly marked and cannot be accepted.
states.success: Show complete audited board, remaining-conflict count, coverage, per-person daily/weekly loading and five participant responses. Label valid awaiting review versus accepted exact revision. Exports state synthetic status, policy, revision, search and review state; acceptance never authorizes executing drills.

persistence: Store versioned fictional inputs, drafts, committed board, policy, reports and exact review record in localStorage on deliberate saves/acceptance; restore on reload, disclose browser-local storage and export. Draft edits are marked Unsaved and preserved during interactions. On storage failure show a warning and permit downloadable review without claiming persistence. Corrupt storage offers explicit reset confirmation. No external file fetch or network dependency.
recovery: Board preview shows saved and draft time/person together. Save or Discard is mandatory before acceptance; saving any input or policy edit invalidates validation/acceptance and requires regeneration or full validation. Resolve conflicts by selecting/editing visible competing values. Missing qualifications, availability, overdue history, budgets and fatigue constraints have editable correction paths. Relaxation requests show old/new values and remain unapplied until a deliberate versioned policy save with reason. Stop preserves inputs. Reset/replacement requires confirmation; no automatic hard-constraint override.
keyboard: Use labeled native inputs, selects, buttons and checkbox; logical Tab order through inputs, optimize/stop, board edits, reports and review. Visible focus; Enter/Space activate native buttons. Focus error summary on failed submissions and announce search/review status with live regions. No drag-only editing; stacked day cards and textual heatmap values at narrow widths. Colors supplement labels; headings and table headers identify all named reports.
